change: the Command Center's Unit 3 rows point at the lesson they name
_context: Three of six Unit 3 rows opened a page about something else: 3.3 Firewalls
opened Wireless, 3.5 IDS opened Firewalls, 3.6 Wireless opened IDS. Rows 3.1,
3.2 and 3.4 were correct throughout, which is why spot-checking missed it: it
is a THREE-CYCLE, not an off-by-one, and only the three lesson BODIES that
swapped handles during the CED renumbering are affected.
The Command Center keys rows on the retired SITE numbers and builds every
handle as lesson-<row number>. That identity was true until three bodies moved.
This ships as a Matrixify sheet and changes no runtime behaviour, so the
second kind here is rederive rather than live: the deployed system has
nothing new to observe until a human imports the sheet.

checks.name: the rewrite is scoped, idempotent, and derived from PLAN
every row's CED number matches what the page it opens says it is
checks._why: Does not read PLAN at all, which is what the generator is built on. It asks each LIVE page what topic it states and compares that to the number the row already prints. Against the current live body this answers 3, which is the defect measured independently of the fix. Runs --fixed so it fetches the live page and applies the relink in memory, rather than depending on a scratch file that would make the gate pass once and then fail on the next run.

checks.name: THE PING-PONG: a three-cycle written as ordered replaces
checks._why: The trap lib/cyber-unit3-renumber.js documents. Rewriting lesson-3 to lesson-5 and then lesson-5 to lesson-6 rotates rows that were already right, and the transform cannot tell its own output from its input.

checks.name: the map is typed by hand instead of derived from PLAN
checks._why: Retyping the Unit 3 mapping is how site 3.3 and 3.4 became each other's CED topics in the first place. One wrong digit here and row 3.5 keeps pointing at Firewalls.
checks.find: for (const p of PLAN) OLD_TO_TARGET[p.oldTopic] = p.target;
checks.expect_failure: OLD_TO_TARGET is derived from PLAN, entry for entry

checks.name: the row scope goes greedy and swallows the rows after it
checks._why: The lazy quantifier is what keeps one row's rewrite inside that row. Greedy, the first row's scope runs to the last site:{ in the array.
checks.expect_failure: data array: all 6 Unit 3 rows point at the right lesson
